title: Give important commands a short persistent operations history
evidence: v065 UI has an internal capped12-message _msg_history and a pending display queue. History is not exposed to players; same-frame/repeated-string events can be lost and urgent events can wait behind routine feedback (HUD15/16).
reproduction: Source walkthrough: deploy, connect, and overclock in sequence; each success replaces the previous message.
impact: Successful operations feel like configuration changes and their causal sequence is easy to lose.
recommendation: Keep three recent high-value command acknowledgements and a brief target-local cue for foothold/session success. Do not log routine packets.
acceptance: Deployment, session establishment and ICE evasion remain reviewable after another action; the feed stays bounded and readable at 200% text.
disposition: Deferred accessible operations-history proposal; v065 already has an internal12-message history. Corrected observation retained in candidates.

title: Allow unwanted contract offers to rotate out
evidence: The board stops generation at three contracts. Deadlines decrease only for accepted contracts; an unaccepted offer has no decline or expiry path and can occupy its slot forever.
reproduction: Source walkthrough: let three offers arrive and leave all unaccepted; generation remains blocked indefinitely.
impact: One poor early assortment can suppress later jobs unless the player accepts an unwanted timed task simply to clear it.
recommendation: Add a low-friction decline or replace-offer action, or expire unaccepted offers after a generous separate lifetime.
acceptance: Three unwanted offers cannot permanently block the board, and refreshing offers does not erase an accepted job's progress.
disposition: Implemented in the final snapshot: contract Decline removes unwanted offers and advances refresh cooldown. Removed from the main count.

title: Gate early offers to achievable resource chains
evidence: _gen_contract can choose Crypto stock from the first offer; no eligibility check examines research, accessible vaults, Tools or the ability to pay for a Skimmer. The first offer arrives after 10 seconds.
reproduction: Source walkthrough: generate a stock contract at the fresh starting state; Crypto remains an equally selectable stock resource despite the unbuilt guarded supply chain.
impact: Early jobs can advertise an attractive reward for a production path that the player cannot reasonably establish within its deadline.
recommendation: Filter starter offers by currently available or imminently affordable production, allowing advanced offers once their chain is demonstrated.
acceptance: Opening offers have a feasible documented route using available tools/resources; advanced Crypto jobs appear after the relevant production path becomes attainable.
disposition: Implemented in the final snapshot: stock offers filter through connected enabled output resources. Remaining deadline/rate balance is retained separately.

title: Tie coverage yield to suitable hosts instead of every nearby building
evidence: _coverage counts any eligible city building inside the disk. _production applies the same multiplier to all producer types without checking the covered block's service or resource.
reproduction: Source walkthrough: compare two producer types placed near the same occupied blocks; both receive the same density multiplier.
impact: Every hack optimises the same geometric building count, weakening the meaning of package registries, mail hosts and cloud targets.
recommendation: When host discovery is introduced, count suitable discovered target classes or apply one clear host affinity; keep the same output resource and radius.
acceptance: Two hack types can have a readable reason to prefer different targets, with eligible coverage visible before commitment and no extra resource type.
disposition: Deferred host-affinity balance change after the discovery prototype.

title: Give Crypto laundering a return profile distinct from Intel sales
evidence: When a processor creates credits, _move_packets applies _market_price regardless of processor type. The Crypto Mixer therefore suffers the same wallet-based saturation as the Darknet Market, although _next_step recommends diversification.
reproduction: Source calculation: a Mixer credit return and a Market credit return at the same Cash balance both receive the same price multiplier.
impact: The expensive Crypto branch changes inputs but does not provide a different answer to falling Intel sale prices.
recommendation: Evaluate a simple distinct laundering payout or saturation curve, or present Crypto honestly as an alternate supply source rather than relief from Intel saturation.
acceptance: The Crypto branch has a documented economic niche demonstrated against a same-cost Intel expansion at mid-to-late Cash balances.
disposition: Deferred optional economy balance experiment.

title: Make starter compute Overclock economics understandable
evidence: Overclock costs 20 Cycles for 20 seconds. A 1.0 coverage Mirai adds 20 gross Cycles before route loss; on a 10-cell DNS route its expected extra delivery is 17 Cycles, below the cost.
reproduction: Source expectation calculation using RATE_NEST=1, multiplier=1, duration=20 and DNS distance loss=10*0.015; this is an expected return, not a played sample.
impact: The first available compute boost can appear to be a recovery tool while worsening the player's Cycles reserve.
recommendation: Show its expected gain and loss, or tune starter-compute cost/duration so an uncongested sustainable route has a clear positive benefit.
acceptance: The command communicates whether extra delivered output is expected to exceed its cost; a starter recovery use has a documented useful case.
disposition: Operating-cost context covered by UI-CONTROLS-14; charging unusable producers covered by SIM17.

title: Choose ICE entry points using exposure as well as path depth
evidence: _launch_sweep picks the connected node with the largest _chain length. It does not consider protocol noise, valuable output, active production or the origin of current Trace.
reproduction: Source walkthrough: compare a long silent chain with a short noisy branch; the longest chain wins target selection regardless of exposure.
impact: Building a deep efficient backbone determines the target more strongly than risky hacking decisions, reducing the strategic relevance of protocol choice.
recommendation: Use a small deterministic exposure score with depth as a tie-breaker and identify the implicated branch in the warning.
acceptance: A documented network example shows that increased exposure changes the entry target predictably without making the warning harder to read or removing pause-safe counterplay.
disposition: Deferred threat-selection experiment until threat feedback is legible.

title: Loaded numeric values lack bounds and can overwrite nodes or create invalid camera state
evidence: A fixture with next_id=1, camera zoom=0 and compute=-100 is accepted with no validation error; _apply_save assigns these values directly. Evidence: simulation_results save_invalid_ranges. The retained behaviour was rechecked in the final code snapshot; stage-named results are probes/simulation_v066_results.json and probes/hud_v066_results.json.
reproduction: Edit these numeric fields in a valid isolated save and validate it. Other bounded fields include size, cap_rate, lane, accumulator and quarantine/boost timers.
impact: The next placement can reuse the hub ID; invalid zoom and negative or extreme simulation values enter a supposedly validated run.
recommendation: Validate finite numeric values and their allowed ranges, require next_id greater than every restored ID, and validate footprint bounds and sizes.
acceptance: Reject nonfinite/out-of-range values and colliding next_id while preserving the current run; all saves generated by normal play pass.
disposition: Merged numeric invariants into SIM02.

title: Save version and researched IDs are trusted without compatibility checks
evidence: Validator accepts version='999.0' and researched=['invalid_tech']; _is_unlocked later indexes TECH[t] without a guard. Evidence: simulation_results save_unknown_version/save_unknown_research. The retained behaviour was rechecked in the final code snapshot; stage-named results are probes/simulation_v066_results.json and probes/hud_v066_results.json.
reproduction: Validate a current save with an unknown version or researched ID. This is a controlled forward-version/damaged-save fixture.
impact: Unsupported saves appear to load successfully and can fail when tool availability is queried.
recommendation: Declare supported save schema versions, migrate known older versions and reject incompatible ones; validate researched IDs or explicitly ignore unknown optional entries.
acceptance: A future schema produces a clear compatibility message; unknown research never causes a dictionary access error; supported older saves migrate correctly.
disposition: Merged schema compatibility and researched IDs into SIM01.

title: Unlimited-time full Undo refunds allow temporary production infrastructure at no capital cost
evidence: Source confirms place/tunnel Undo refunds complete cost and has no elapsed-time or produced-output condition; production earnings are retained. Undo stack is limited by20 actions, not time. No abuse playthrough is claimed. The retained behaviour was rechecked in the final code snapshot; stage-named results are probes/simulation_v066_results.json and probes/hud_v066_results.json.
reproduction: Build a small producer and tunnel, allow it to earn while making no new undoable actions, then Undo both.
impact: Full construction refunds undermine investment tradeoffs and can make temporary infrastructure economically free.
recommendation: Playtest a short full-refund grace period, followed by explicit salvage value, while retaining easy correction of immediate placement mistakes.
acceptance: Immediate accidental placement remains reversible at full cost; established earning infrastructure follows a clearly shown salvage policy.
disposition: Deferred Undo economic-policy decision; free temporary production may be intentional in a planning game.

title: Disabling a processor has no explicit policy for already travelling inputs
evidence: Controlled in-flight fixture: send Intel toward Forge, Disable Forge before arrival, then advance packets; Tools still increases1 although on=false. Inputs/fuel are paid at dispatch, so completing queued work may be intentional. Evidence: simulation_results disabled_inflight_converter. The retained behaviour was rechecked in the final code snapshot; stage-named results are probes/simulation_v066_results.json and probes/hud_v066_results.json.
reproduction: Disable a Forge/Lab/Mixer while its input packet is travelling from C2.
impact: 'Disabled' leaves players unsure whether production stops immediately or accepted work finishes; hidden queued work complicates resource planning.
recommendation: Specify finish-queued-work or immediate-stop behavior. If finishing work, show pending conversions and 'stopping after current inputs'; if stopping immediately, define input/fuel refund or loss.
acceptance: Inspector and action text explain the chosen pending-work policy; input and fuel accounting remain conserved under Disable, removal and reroute.
disposition: Deferred policy clarification for in-flight inputs; do not call a currently unspecified rule a bug.

title: Goal-fixed chart scaling hides early economic changes
evidence: graph.gd maps balance to GOAL_CREDITS=1000 across a90px chart. A20-Cash movement uses only1.8px; values beyond the goal clamp at the top. The scale is source-confirmed; this is a proposed readability change. The retained behaviour was rechecked in the final code snapshot; stage-named results are probes/simulation_v066_results.json and probes/hud_v066_results.json.
reproduction: Compare early balances0–50 or continue after reaching1000 Cash.
impact: The chart is nearly flat during the opening and loses information after victory, when players most need evidence that production works.
recommendation: Provide an adaptive observed-range scale or selectable goal/balance views, retaining a clear goal reference.
acceptance: Early20-Cash changes are visibly distinguishable and post-goal balances are readable, with scale labels preventing misleading comparisons.
disposition: Merged adaptive chart scaling into HUD07.

title: DDoS recovery is buried in Stats and remains an enabled action when unaffordable
evidence: The Smokescreen button is created only inside stats_box, connects directly toscrub_trace and has no update gating for cost; source and screenshot10_stats.png show a cost label clipped at the panel edge. Functional quarantine semantics are separately covered bySIM16. The retained behaviour was rechecked in the final code snapshot; stage-named results are probes/simulation_v066_results.json and probes/hud_v066_results.json.
reproduction: When a sweep arrives, locate the counteraction while viewing Build or an inspector; repeat with insufficient Cycles/Tools.
impact: A time-critical action requires tab navigation and trial-clicking to learn why it is unavailable.
recommendation: Expose a contextual Smokescreen action alongside threat diagnostics, with complete readable cost, affordability and effect preview; keep Stats access as a secondary location.
acceptance: The player can find the available counteraction during the warning, and insufficient resources are explained before spending/clicking.
disposition: Deferred separate DDoS discoverability proposal; retained SIM16 also includes its cost/access context as a follow-up.

title: Continue provides no description of the saved run
evidence: Continue is a single static button whose enabled state comes from Session.has_save(); no timestamp, seed, progress or saved-run summary is presented. Save validation/backup bugs are owned by the simulation audit, not this item.
reproduction: Return after several sessions and inspect Continue before loading.
impact: Players cannot confirm which run they will resume or whether it is the expected save.
recommendation: Show a concise save preview with save time and meaningful run progress, plus an explanatory empty state when no save exists.
acceptance: Before continuing, the saved run can be identified from its timestamp/progress; preview failure never blocks valid backup recovery.
disposition: Deferred saved-run preview.

title: Accessibility settings cannot be opened before starting a game
evidence: The startup menu offers only New Game, Continue and Quit. Settings is constructed in ui.gd after the main scene opens, so a first-time user cannot choose reduced motion or enlarged text from the entry screen.
reproduction: Start without a saved preference file and look for accessibility controls before choosing New Game.
impact: Players must navigate and view the game with default presentation before they can configure it.
recommendation: Expose the shared Settings panel from the startup menu, applying options immediately to the startup scene as appropriate.
acceptance: A first launch allows changing motion, contrast, palette, packet style and text size without creating or loading a run.
disposition: Implemented in the final snapshot: Accessibility is available from the startup menu, with a live preview. Removed from the main count.

title: Load Game remains available when there is no save to load
evidence: Startup Continue is disabled based on Session.has_save, but Menu/Pause Load Game is always an active button connected directly to main.load_game. No corresponding availability state or reason is supplied.
reproduction: Start a fresh isolated game with no primary/backup save and open Menu or Pause.
impact: The menu presents an unavailable operation and defers the explanation until the player invokes it.
recommendation: Reflect save availability consistently in Load Game controls and explain the unavailable state, refreshing after Save or external save changes.
acceptance: Without a primary or valid backup, Load is visibly unavailable with a readable reason; saving enables it, and usable backup recovery remains available.
disposition: Deferred empty-save affordance.

title: Settings options lack descriptions of their visible effects
evidence: Settings contains only option labels and short values such as On/Off or Code/Dots. There are no explanatory tooltips, descriptions or previews for what motion is reduced, what contrast changes, or what packet Code/Dots means.
reproduction: Open Settings and compare Packet style, Reduced motion and High contrast before changing them.
impact: Players must experiment to learn whether an option addresses their readability or motion needs.
recommendation: Add concise descriptions or previews of each option's user-visible scope, including that motion reduction preserves the information needed to follow traffic.
acceptance: Every option's effect can be understood before activation; descriptions remain accessible at200% and through keyboard focus.
disposition: Deferred settings explanatory copy.

title: Text size is a hidden cyclic sequence rather than a directly selectable value
evidence: _toggle_setting('ts') advances100→125→150→175→200→100. The control shows only the current value, so reaching a smaller adjacent size can require cycling through every larger value and an abrupt reset.
reproduction: Choose150%, then try reducing to125% or previewing several values.
impact: Adjusting readability is slower and the wraparound is undisclosed.
recommendation: Use a labelled choice list or bounded decrease/increase controls with an explicit default/reset action.
acceptance: Any supported value can be selected directly or with predictable bounded steps; increasing at200% never silently jumps to100%.
disposition: Deferred direct text-scale selector after layouts work at every existing scale.

title: Output adjustment buttons remain enabled at their limits
evidence: Main clamps cap_rate to0..1, but _update_info never updates rate_down/rate_up disabled states. Probe reports minus enabled at0% and plus enabled at100%, so these presses generate messages without changing output.
reproduction: Select a producer at100% and press+, or reduce it to0% and press−.
impact: The control offers an action that has no effect and obscures the supported output range.
recommendation: Disable the appropriate endpoint button and identify the range/step size in its help; provide explicit accessible names for increase/decrease.
acceptance: Minus is unavailable at0%, plus at100%, and adjustments between boundaries clearly move by25 percentage points.
disposition: Deferred limit-button polish.

title: Tunnel overload advice has no contextual upgrade or reroute action
evidence: The overload text recommends a fatter tunnel or alternate route, but the selected-tunnel branch exposes only remove_btn. Improving the link requires dismantling it, re-opening Build→Links, reselecting endpoints and rebuilding.
reproduction: Select an overloaded DNS tunnel and follow the inspector's recommendation to use a higher-capacity tunnel.
impact: Diagnosing a bottleneck is separated from the corrective action by several navigation and placement steps.
recommendation: Offer an Upgrade/Reroute flow from the selected link with protocol metrics, cost and route preview, committing atomically with undo support.
acceptance: A selected bottleneck can be upgraded/rerouted from its inspector; a failed or cancelled preview preserves the existing connection and resources.
disposition: Deferred separate contextual-action proposal; HUD11 includes upgrade/reroute affordances as follow-up work after selecting the diagnostic link.

title: The Proc category label does not explain what it contains
evidence: The visible subcategory labels are Hacks/Proc/Links and Proc has no tooltip or introductory label. Its contents are processors plus Proxy conversion.
reproduction: Open Build and look at the Proc subcategory as a first-time player.
impact: A central resource-conversion action is behind an unexplained abbreviation.
recommendation: Use a readable category name such as Processing and provide a brief category description, adapting layout at large text sizes.
acceptance: The category meaning is apparent from its visible label or immediate help; names remain fully readable at supported text scales.
disposition: Deferred Proc abbreviation polish.

title: Arming a tool removes the palette needed to choose the next tool
evidence: show_info becomes true whenever current_tool is nonempty and hides build_scroll/build_cat_row. To switch tools the player must re-enter Build (which clears current_tool) before selecting a different row.
reproduction: Arm Phishing Kit, then attempt to immediately choose DNS Tunnel from the left panel.
impact: A repeated build→connect sequence needs a navigation reset between actions.
recommendation: Keep a compact tool switcher or an explicit Back to tools action beside the armed-tool help.
acceptance: From an armed tool the next available tool can be selected directly, with the pending link/placement state cancelled consistently.
disposition: Deferred armed-tool switching convenience.

title: A prerequisite-locked research card hides its Research cost
evidence: For a not-ready technology _process replaces the entire button with Locked—needs <name>. The cost is only rendered in the ready branch, and _tech_row has no separate cost label. HTTP/2 costs25RP but that amount is hidden before Exploit Development.
reproduction: Before researching Exploit Development, inspect HTTP/2 Flooding and plan total Research needed for the two-step path.
impact: Players cannot budget the next unlock chain from the Tech panel.
recommendation: Display cost independently of the current action state, together with prerequisite requirements.
acceptance: A locked, affordable, unaffordable or completed technology consistently exposes its defined cost; the Exploits→HTTP/2 path can be budgeted before either purchase.
disposition: Merged locked-card cost visibility into UI-PANELS-13.

title: Research list keeps completed and unavailable cards ahead of actionable ones
evidence: Tech rows are created once in TECH dictionary insertion order and all remain visible; _process updates button text/state but provides no filter or prioritization.
reproduction: Research several early entries, then revisit Tech at200% text to locate remaining affordable research lower in the list.
impact: Repeated scrolling through already-completed cards slows progression planning.
recommendation: Offer stable Available/All/Researched filters or group actionable and completed technologies while preserving keyboard focus.
acceptance: Remaining eligible technologies can be viewed without scrolling through completed cards, and the full dependency/cost history remains accessible.
disposition: Deferred research sorting polish.

title: Accepted-job countdown shows zero before the deadline expires
evidence: The UI casts remaining deadline to int, flooring any positive fraction below1 to0. The evaluator expires only when deadline<=0, so a still-active job displays0s left.
reproduction: Observe an accepted contract when deadline is between0 and1 seconds.
impact: The timer reports expiry early and makes a last-second completion look inconsistent.
recommendation: Use ceil for a remaining-seconds countdown, or show a sub-second format near expiry.
acceptance: Every positive remaining deadline displays at least1s in the integer countdown;0/expired is reserved for actual expiry.
disposition: Merged sub-second deadline formatting into UI-PANELS-20.

title: Contract deadline has no urgency state
evidence: All status labels receive the same green font colour at creation; _process updates text without changing appearance as a deadline approaches. There is no imminent-expiry cue beyond the decreasing number.
reproduction: Compare an accepted card with90 seconds remaining to the same card with5 seconds remaining.
impact: A time-critical task looks like ordinary healthy status and is easy to miss while managing the network.
recommendation: Introduce readable soon/urgent deadline states with text or an icon as well as colour, respecting reduced-motion settings.
acceptance: Near-expiry thresholds are evident without relying solely on colour or animation; completed/unaccepted cards are not marked urgent.
disposition: Merged deadline urgency into UI-PANELS-20.

title: Reverse processor packets draw their code trail ahead of their movement
evidence: For dir=-1, along=total-dist decreases as the packet moves, but the trail always samples along-7 and along-14. Those samples lead a reverse packet rather than trail it; forward packets use the same expression correctly.
reproduction: Enable code packet style, zoom above 0.8, and watch a processor-input packet moving outward from C2. Source example: along=60 samples 53/46, both ahead of decreasing along.
impact: The visual motion cue can imply the wrong direction for the input leg of a processor round trip.
recommendation: Offset trail samples behind the packet according to its direction, preserving the resource shape and Reduced Motion behaviour.
acceptance: Code trails sit behind both C2-bound output packets and outward processor-input packets on horizontal, vertical and turning routes.
disposition: Deferred cosmetic reverse-packet trail defect; movement itself is not claimed incorrect.
